limits: TlsAlloc is a modeled physical service: physical TLS-index allocation returns a distinct live index or 0xffffffff on exhaustion.
TlsGetValue is a modeled physical service: physical TLS lookup uses both the current thread and allocated index, returning the stored pointer or null.
TlsSetValue is a modeled physical service: physical TLS publication stores the exact container pointer only on success; a failed return leaves TLS unchanged.
InitializeCriticalSection is a modeled physical service: physical initialization of the exact 24-byte critical-section record, with nonreturning service exceptions.
EnterCriticalSection is a modeled physical service: physical lock acquisition tracks section identity, owner and recursion.
LeaveCriticalSection is a modeled physical service: physical lock release balances the current owner and section.
GlobalAlloc is a modeled physical service: physical movable global allocation preserves exact flags and separate handle/data identities; failure returns null.
GlobalHandle is a modeled physical service: physical conversion from a global data pointer to its handle also accepts null on initial allocation failure.
GlobalUnlock is a modeled physical service: physical handle unlock decrements its lock count; zero can be a successful final unlock.
GlobalReAlloc is a modeled physical service: physical movable global reallocation preserves the prefix and preserves old ownership on failure.
GlobalLock is a modeled physical service: physical handle lock returns its data pointer; the cached IAT target remains this same physical import.
LocalAlloc is a modeled physical service: physical local allocation returns live memory or null; flags 0x40 zero bytes, while flags zero do not promise initialized contents.
LocalReAlloc is a modeled physical service: physical fixed-block reallocation with flags 2 preserves the old prefix and keeps the old allocation alive on failure.

RaiseException is a modeled physical service: physical noncontinuable exception boundary: flags 1 must Halt without returning, reached through unchanged original throw helpers; no exception dispatch is fabricated.
The caller-supplied factory is a genuine cdecl callback with no arguments; original MFC factory bodies remain original when supplied, and are never replaced with game-state fixtures.
Failure evidence ends at nonreturning RaiseException and does not establish Windows exception dispatch, hidden-frame unwinding, lock cleanup or app-side exception support.
Owned functions retain all 119 and 227 original bytes; only two separately proven two-byte instruction ranges are exempt from required execution.
Cases require live backing for every indexed access, including the original unchecked final store for an out-of-logical-range zero value; no bounds correction is part of this family.
Optional source capability observes all eleven CPU fields and the entire bounded stack; getter preserves FS and setter preserves EBX, EBP and FS over supported backed aliases.

Source callback capability is finite and argument-selected: original0x502335,0x502369 and0x502301 execute whole at CALL0x5033ba/return0x5033be; this does not grant arbitrary callback authority or establish complete CWinApp/startup execution.
The nested owned setter must execute its translated complete source body at the real child frame and return PC; no context-free shortcut or original-setter bridge establishes that translation.
Existing compiled integration metadata concerns the prior ordinary implementation and does not establish the optional source extension or native cold TLS composition.

The optional source domain inherits prepend0x502f26 preservation0x472 and excludes aliases that overwrite its saved ESI; the real cold manager link offset4 satisfies that contract, while ordinary behavior remains unchanged.

Application factory allocation0x84 and record spans are fresh and disjoint from active controls and saved restoration slots, preserving its declared0x472 contract. Genuine TLS consumers return at0x50229e and0x5025cf; reaching the latter does not execute its CWinApp publication instruction.
